title: review: B2 v3: compact delta packets in planner_runs — decision_packet/grouped_packet delegate to planner_packet.build with changes since the previous decision, structured scout findings, memory titles; escalation packet on re-escalation; packet size into telemetry (P4, P10)
spec:
Why: planner_runs.decision_packet (planner_runs.py:43-107) and grouped_packet (1063-1090) rebuild a per-point packet with the full spawn packet inventory and 300-char scout summaries, no delta, no memory, no required-output section. planner_packet (merged) provides build(sections, *, goal, previous, changes, scout_findings, memory_hits, cap_chars) -> {text, chars, est_tokens, hash, sections, truncated, delta} and escalation_packet(...); B1 v3 (T-0741, merged) made run_group sections 4-tuples (point, ctx, route, classification) and records launch rows. Spec reviews of T-0743 and T-0747 folded in: rewritten DecisionPacket tests, direct events-table scan, _decision_task for purged held tasks, memory_recall()["hits"], no module-level packet state. The Planner waived a third spec review.
What (planner_runs.py; tests in tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py, tests/test_goals.py, tests/test_planner_runs.py):
- _packet_sections(sections) -> list of planner_packet section dicts: for each (point, ctx, route, classification): task = _decision_task(point["goal_id"], point["kind"], point["payload_key"]) (existing helper, purged task -> None, never raises); reviews = [{path, line, issue} for every comment in failures.rejecting_reviews(task)] (max 10) when task; failures = the text of (task.resume_hint or task.result).failures when task; depends_on_statuses = [{id, status} for dep in task.depends_on via bus.get, KeyError -> status "missing"].
- _previous_launch(goal_id) -> the planner_runs record of this goal with the latest started_at that has a launch_id, or None.
- _changes_since(goal_id, cursor) -> list of {"task", "field", "from", "to", "ts"}: query the sqlite events table directly under bus.locked() — `select task_id, seq, ts, data from events where seq > ? and task_id in (<the goal id and its children ids>) order by seq` (parameterised, ids from bus.read() filtered by parent == goal_id) — never through bus.events and its global 200-row page; for each row's data dict, fields status, hold_reason, merged_into only; from = the previous value seen in the scan (None when unknown), to = new; keep the last 20 entries (newest last). cursor = previous["cursor_at_launch"].
- _scout_findings(goal_id) -> scout_evidence.normalize_findings(scout result) concatenated over the goal's done scout children (max 10, highest confidence first); _memory_hits(goal) -> up to 10 {"title": hit title} from scout_evidence.memory_recall(goal title, root=STATE)["hits"] (the same ["hits"] extraction spawn.py uses), guarded by try/except Exception -> [].
- _build_grouped(sections) -> (text, meta): meta is the full planner_packet.build result; build(_packet_sections(sections), goal=bus.get(goal_id), previous={"state_version": prev.get("state_version")} if prev else None, changes=_changes_since(goal_id, prev["cursor_at_launch"]) if prev else None, scout_findings=_scout_findings(goal_id), memory_hits=_memory_hits(goal), cap_chars=[planner].decision_packet_chars default 6000). grouped_packet(sections) -> _build_grouped(sections)[0] (public, text only). run_group calls _build_grouped directly, stores meta chars/hash/delta/truncated on the records as packet_chars, packet_hash, packet_delta, packet_truncated and passes packet_chars=meta["chars"] to planner_telemetry.record_launch (replacing len(prompt)); no module-level mutable state. decision_packet(goal_id, kind, payload, repo_path) (legacy single-point path) builds one section via build_ctx + planner_taxonomy.classify and returns build(...)["text"] (len <= cap); the legacy inventory, "Task title:"/"Scout summaries:"/"Spawn packet:" lines and 300-char summaries are removed. Rewrite tests/test_goals.py's DecisionPacket suite (lines ~616-707) to the new format: same scenarios, assertions on the planner_packet section headings (Decision, Goal, Relevant task state, Scout findings, Required output), the fenced untrusted text, and len(text) <= cap; keep the test method names.
- Escalation (P10): in run_group, when ctx.get("reescalation") is True and a planner_shadow row exists for this goal's previous launch (rows of runs/sched/planner_shadow.jsonl with goal_id, latest started_at), render the prompt from planner_packet.escalation_packet(goal=..., original_sections=..., opus_decision={proposed_action, summary, tasks_proposed, confidence, needs_fable, unresolved} from that row, unresolved=row unresolved, conflicting_evidence=None, scout_findings, memory_hits, reason=";".join(hard_reasons), cap_chars) instead of build; store packet_kind "escalation" vs "decision" on the planner_runs records (the launch row is unchanged).
- The rendered prompt still goes through spawn.render("planner-decision", packet=text).
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_first_decision_packet_has_sections_and_no_inventory — grouped_packet for a scouts_done goal with two done scouts and memory_recall patched to return the real dict shape {hits: [...]} yields text containing 'first Planner decision for this goal', the Scout findings and Memory sections (with the hit titles), no 'Spawn packet' section, and len(text) <= decision_packet_chars

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_delta_packet_reads_events_table_beyond_200_rows — after a first launch record with cursor_at_launch, 250 unrelated events on another goal followed by a child task changing status and hold_reason still produce a packet whose Changes section lists both fields with from/to and the previous state_version; the record stores packet_delta True and packet_chars equal to the build's chars, and the launch row's packet_chars matches

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_held_section_tolerates_purged_task_and_renders_evidence — a held task with resume_hint failures, a rejecting review with two comments and one missing dependency renders failures (capped), the two comments as path:line issue, and 'missing' for the dependency; a held point whose task file was deleted builds a packet with task state absent instead of raising

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_escalation_packet_used_on_reescalation — with ctx reescalation True and a prior planner_shadow row for the goal, the rendered prompt contains 'Escalation reason:' and 'Opus proposed decision', no 'Changes since previous decision' section, and the record has packet_kind escalation; without a shadow row the ordinary build is used

tests/test_goals.py::test_decision_packet_new_format — the rewritten DecisionPacket suite passes against planner_packet output (section headings present, untrusted hold_reason fenced, len(text) <= cap, no Spawn packet inventory) and the whole tests/test_goals.py module is green

result.summary: Traced the full diff against the packet spec: _packet_sections, _previous_launch, _changes_since (parameterized SQL under bus.locked(), never bus.events, last-20 trim), _scout_findings/_memory_hits, _build_grouped/grouped_packet, decision_packet legacy path, and the run_group escalation branch all match the acceptance criteria. Verified bus.locked() is reentrant per-thread so the nested lock in _changes_since (called while run_group already holds the lock) is not a deadlock. Verified packet_text/packet_meta are set on every path before use (no UnboundLocalError), _previous_launch is computed before the current record is stamped with launch_id (no self-reference), scout finding confidence is always a float (safe sort), and purged-task handling (_decision_task, _packet_tasks fallback) matches the 'never raise' contract. Only two low-severity cleanliness nits found: a dead _fenced helper and a duplicated _SAFE_KEY check.

comments.issue: _fenced helper now has zero callers after the packet rewrite delegates fencing to planner_packet.build — dead code, should be removed.
_SAFE_KEY validation of goal_id/kind/payload_key is duplicated verbatim (once before packet building, once unchanged before handover.write). Harmless but redundant; collapse to one check.
